channel.title: Kia recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Kia EV9 air bag may not detect a child
item.description: Kia America is recalling certain 2025-2026 EV9 vehicles. Because of improper routing, the system meant to detect a child or child seat in the front passenger seat and turn off the air bag may not work as intended, so the air bag may not deactivate when it should.

item.title: Kia EV6, EV9 Battery Fire Risk
item.description: The high voltage battery in these vehicles may contain cells with parts that are out of alignment inside them. This can lead to a fire while the vehicle is parked or being driven. Kia will replace the entire battery system to fix the problem.

item.title: Kia Telluride Power Seat Motor Fire Risk
item.description: The motor that powers the front seat may overheat if the seat slide knob gets stuck, or if an earlier repair for this same problem was done incorrectly. This overheating can lead to a fire while the vehicle is parked or being driven. This recall replaces an earlier one for the same issue, so even vehicles that already had that repair done will need this new fix completed as well.

item.title: Kia Carnival Fuel Pipe Connection May Leak
item.description: Kia is recalling certain Carnival vehicles because fuel may leak at the connection between the fuel pipe and the fuel rail. A fuel leak like this increases the risk of a fire.

item.title: Kia Telluride Seat Frame May Not Restrain Occupant
item.description: These Kia Telluride vehicles have power front seats. Because of a manufacturing error, the frame inside the driver and passenger seat backs may not hold up the way it should. If the vehicle is in a crash, a weakened seat back frame may fail to properly hold the occupant in place. This increases the chance that a person in the seat could be hurt during a crash.

item.title: Kia Instrument Panel Display May Fail
item.description: A software error on certain Kia vehicles, including the K4 and Sorento, may cause the instrument panel display to fail.

item.title: Kia Sportage Instrument Panel Screen May Fail
item.description: Kia America is recalling certain Sportage and Sportage PHEV vehicles equipped with a 4.2-inch instrument screen and a genuine Kia tow hitch wiring harness accessory. In these vehicles, a software error can cause the instrument panel screen to stop working properly. When that happens, the driver may not be able to see important safety information on the screen, such as the speedometer or warning lights.

item.title: Kia K5 Fuel Tank Damage Risk of Fire
item.description: Kia says a damaged check valve in some K5 vehicles can let air get into the fuel tank. That extra air can make the tank expand, and the expanded tank can touch hot parts of the exhaust system. Contact with the hot exhaust can melt the fuel tank, so Kia is having dealers check and fix the part before that happens.

item.title: Kia Telluride Spare Tire May Impair Braking
item.description: These vehicles come with an incorrect spare tire. If that spare tire is installed, it can impair the anti-lock braking system and the traction control system.

item.title: Kia Sorento Blower Motor Wiring Fire Risk
item.description: On these Kia Sorento vehicles, the wiring for the heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) blower motor may not be adequate. This wiring problem can result in a fire. Dealers will replace the wiring harness and the blower motor resistor so this cannot happen.

item.title: Kia K4, Sorento Engine Bolts May Loosen
item.description: The bolts that hold the connecting rods inside the engine may not have been tightened correctly when these vehicles were built. Because those bolts aren't secure, the engine's internal parts aren't held together the way they should be. This can cause the engine to suddenly lose the power that keeps the vehicle moving forward, and that loss of power can happen at any time while you're driving.

item.title: Kia Telluride door trim molding can peel off vehicle
item.description: Kia is recalling certain Telluride SUVs. The belt molding trim on the doors can separate into layers and come off the vehicle. Dealers will inspect the belt molding trim and replace it where necessary, at no charge. Kia mailed owner notification letters on November 19, 2025. Owners who have questions can contact Kia customer service and refer to the company's number for this recall, SC347.

item.title: Kia K5 rear window trim may loosen and detach
item.description: Kia is recalling certain K5 sedans. The trim pieces along the left and right rear windows may work loose and come off the car. Dealers will inspect the trim on the rear roof pillars and replace it if needed, at no charge. Kia mailed owner notification letters on November 19, 2025. Owners who have questions can contact Kia customer service and refer to the company's number for this recall, SC346.

item.title: Kia K5 Parking Lights May Flicker From Software Error
item.description: A software error in the K5's Power-net Domain Controller (PDC) may cause the parking lights to flicker instead of staying lit properly. Parking lights that don't illuminate the way they should can make the vehicle harder for other drivers to see.

item.title: Kia EV9 Rear Drive Motor Weld Failure Risk
item.description: In some Kia EV9 vehicles, the motor shaft inside the rear gear drive unit may have been welded incorrectly. Over time, this faulty weld can cause the shaft to become damaged. If that happens, the vehicle can lose the power that drives the wheels while you are driving. Dealers will replace the entire rear gear drive unit, and the repair will be done free of charge.

item.title: Kia Seltos and Soul Engine Piston Rings Defective
item.description: Certain Kia Seltos and Soul vehicles may have piston oil rings that weren't manufactured correctly. Over time, this can cause damage inside the engine. If the engine is damaged, it may stall unexpectedly while you're driving, or in some cases catch fire. Either of these increases the chance of a crash or of someone being injured.

item.title: Kia Niro Seat Wiring May Disable Air Bags
item.description: Certain Kia Niro EV, plug-in hybrid, and hybrid vehicles have a wiring assembly beneath the front passenger seat that may become damaged. If that happens, the front air bags and seat belts may not deploy the way they're supposed to in a crash. It could also cause the side curtain air bag to deploy on its own, without any crash happening.

item.title: Kia Sorento may lose headlights and taillights
item.description: This recall affects certain Kia Sorento, Sorento Hybrid, and Sorento Plug-In Hybrid vehicles. A software error in the vehicle's body control computer may cause the low-beam headlights and taillights to stop working.

item.title: Kia EV9 Missing Rear Seat Mounting Bolts
item.description: Some Kia EV9 SUVs may be missing the bolts that hold down the second-row and third-row seats. These bolts are what secure the seats to the vehicle. If a seat is missing its mounting bolts, it may not stay properly secured, so it might not restrain a passenger the way it should, increasing the risk of injury.

item.title: Kia EV6 Charging Unit May Cause Power Loss
item.description: Kia America is recalling certain EV6 vehicles because a part called the Integrated Charging Control Unit, which helps charge the car's 12-volt battery, may become damaged and stop working. When this happens, the 12-volt battery stops charging, and the vehicle can lose drive power while it is being driven.

item.title: Kia EV9 Instrument Screen Can Go Blank
item.description: Kia is recalling certain EV9 vehicles because of a software error. The instrument panel screen, which shows the speedometer, warning lights, and other important driving information, can fail and go blank while the vehicle is being driven. When this happens, the driver no longer has access to that safety information on the display.

item.title: Kia EV9 Remote Parking Assist Software Error
item.description: On certain 2024 Kia EV9 vehicles, a software error can affect the remote smart parking assist feature, which lets the driver move the vehicle remotely without being inside it. Because of this error, the feature may miscalculate how much distance the vehicle needs in order to come to a stop. This means the vehicle may not stop exactly where the software expects it to while being operated remotely.

item.title: Sportage Power Steering May Short Circuit
item.description: On certain Sportage vehicles, the circuit board in the power steering assembly may short circuit. If this happens, the vehicle can lose power steering assist. Losing power steering assist increases the risk of a crash.

item.title: Kia Telluride Seat Knob Overheating Fire Risk
item.description: The motor that powers the front seat may overheat if the seat slide knob becomes stuck. This overheating can start a fire, whether the vehicle is parked or being driven. Kia will install a bracket for the seat switch covers and replace the slide knobs to fix the problem.

item.title: Kia EV9 ceiling lining may not absorb crash impact
item.description: Kia is recalling certain EV9 vehicles because the headliner, the padded lining on the inside of the roof, may not protect people well enough if they strike it in a crash. The lining is supposed to absorb some of that impact. Because it may not do so, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule on occupant protection in interior impacts. Dealers will replace the impact-absorbing plates attached to the headliner.

item.title: Kia EV9 Front Passenger Seat Belt Defect
item.description: On some Kia EV9 vehicles, the cover on the front passenger seat belt retractor may not be secured correctly. This can stop the seat belt's automatic locking and emergency locking features from working as they're supposed to. Because of this, the vehicles don't meet federal seat belt safety requirements.

item.title: Kia Sorento Wiring May Cause Steering Loss
item.description: Some Kia Sorento vehicles may have a wiring harness for the power steering system that was assembled incorrectly. This wiring problem can cause the vehicle to lose power steering assist while it is being driven. Without power steering assist, the vehicle becomes harder to steer, and this increases the risk of a crash.

item.title: Kia EV9, Niro EV Differential Gear Bolt Problem
item.description: Kia is recalling certain 2023 Niro EV and 2024 EV9 vehicles. The bolts that hold the gear drive unit in the differential may not have been tightened properly. If this happens, the vehicle could lose its drive power, meaning it stops being able to move under its own power, or the differential could lock up while the vehicle is being driven. This is part of the system that sends power to the wheels.

item.title: Kia Forte Front Control Arm Weld Failure
item.description: Some Kia Forte vehicles have a right front lower control arm that may have been improperly welded. This weld problem can cause the control arm to fail.

item.title: Kia Telluride driveshaft can cause vehicle rollaway
item.description: Kia is recalling certain Telluride SUVs because a component called the intermediate shaft and the right front driveshaft may not be fully engaged with each other. When this happens, the connection between the transmission and the front wheels can come loose enough that the vehicle is able to roll away on its own while it's shifted into Park, even after the driver has stepped out of the vehicle.

item.title: Kia EV6 Charging Unit May Cause Power Loss
item.description: On certain 2022-2024 Kia EV6 vehicles, a part called the Integrated Charging Control Unit can become damaged and stop charging the vehicle's 12-volt battery. When the 12-volt battery isn't being charged properly, the vehicle can lose drive power while it is being driven. Kia is recalling these vehicles to inspect the charging unit and replace it and its fuse if needed, and to update the unit's software.

item.title: Kia K900 and Stinger Turbo Oil Leak Risk
item.description: On certain Kia K900 and Stinger vehicles with the 3.3-liter turbocharged engine, the oil feed pipe and hose that supply oil to the left turbocharger can wear out over time. This can cause the pipe and hose to leak engine oil. Because this leak happens near hot parts of the engine, it raises the chance of a fire starting in the engine compartment while the car is being driven.

item.title: Kia Telluride High Beam Headlights May Fail
item.description: On some Kia Telluride vehicles, the high beam headlights may stop working. This means the high beams might not turn on or work correctly when the driver tries to use them at the front of the vehicle. This issue is limited to the high beam function of the headlights and does not describe any other headlight or lighting problems on the vehicle.

item.title: Kia Telluride Engine Valve Springs May Break
item.description: Kia is recalling certain Telluride SUVs because the engine valve springs may break while the vehicle is being driven. If a valve spring breaks, the engine can suddenly lose the power that drives the wheels, meaning the vehicle can lose forward power unexpectedly while on the road. In some cases, a broken valve spring can also punch a hole through the engine block itself.

item.title: Kia EV6 and Niro EV Drive Shaft Failure
item.description: On certain Niro EV and EV6 vehicles, one of the drive shafts may not have been properly hardened during manufacturing. This can cause the shaft to break while the vehicle is being driven, which results in a sudden loss of power to the wheels. Losing power to the wheels while on the road increases the chance of a crash for the driver and others on the road.

item.title: Kia Carnival and Sportage: Roof Molding May Detach
item.description: The molding along the roof of these vehicles may come loose and fall off while driving. A piece of molding that detaches on the road can become a hazard for other drivers. Dealers will inspect the roof molding and either secure it or replace it, at no cost to owners.

item.title: Kia Soul and Seltos Side Airbags May Deploy Unexpectedly
item.description: In some Kia Soul and Kia Seltos vehicles, a manufacturing error can cause the side curtain airbags to deploy unexpectedly. This means an airbag could inflate at a time when it isn't meant to, rather than only when needed to protect occupants in a crash. This issue can involve the side curtain airbag module on either side of the vehicle.

item.title: Kia Soul EV Parking Mechanism May Be Damaged
item.description: On certain Soul EV vehicles, the mechanism that holds the vehicle in place when the gear shift is set to Park can become damaged. Kia says that if this happens, the vehicle can move on its own even while in Park, if the parking brake isn't also applied and the vehicle is powered on.

item.title: Kia Forte Front Control Arm Weld May Fail
item.description: Kia is recalling certain Forte vehicles because the right front lower control arm may have been welded incorrectly, which can cause it to fail.

item.title: Kia Sorento Rearview Camera May Lose Image
item.description: Due to a manufacturing error, water may get into the rearview camera. When this happens, the camera image may not appear on the vehicle's display screen, so the driver cannot see behind the vehicle using that screen.
